title: Bitcoin analysts predict $300,000–$500,000 price in 2029. The math says no
summary: Title: Bitcoin halving cycle history challenges $300,000–$500,000 moonshot forecasts URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/07/10/bitcoin-analysts-predict-usd300-000-usd500-000-price-in-2029-the-math-says-no Published Time: 2026-07-11T02:30:00.000Z Markdown Content: Updated Jul 11, 2026, 3:03 a.m. Published Jul 11, 2026, 2:30 a.m. 3 min read ![Image 1: Halving cycle data challenges moonshot predictions. (Getty Images)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Fc7d242469e65ee7e6f0e9ceac50286334728802f-5458x3638.jpg%3Fauto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) Halving cycle data challenges moonshot predictions. (Getty Images) Summary * Bitcoin’s historic four-year halving cycles are still producing new highs, but each bull market peak has delivered smaller multiples than the last. * Forecasts calling for bitcoin to reach $300,000 to $500,000 by the next cycle peak in 2029 may be overly optimistic given the shrinking peak-to-peak returns and the asset’s growing size. * As institutional participation, ETFs, and sophisticated derivatives deepen the market, bitcoin is becoming larger, more liquid and less volatile, suggesting the era of parabolic “moonshot” rallies may be over. Crypto analysts are already looking at how high bitcoin [BTC$64,043.04](https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin) could rally in the next cycle, expected to begin later this year, with ambitious targets ranging from $300,000 to $500,000. But one important data point runs counter to those forecasts, suggesting that gains may be more measured than ever. Unlike gold or stocks, bitcoin tends to move in clear four-year cycles centered on the mining reward halving, an event that halves the amount of new bitcoin produced per block every 4 years.
